d.d: A type of one-eared spade used in Ireland.
Having or demonstrating undivided and constant support for someone or something.
d.x: Dogs are very loyal animals, which is why they make wonderful pets.

d.d: Firm in allegiance to a person or institution; allegiant.
Faithful to a person or cause.
d.x: We must remain loyal to the mission.

d.d: A person who is loyal to a cause, generally used as a political affiliation.
A person from the 13 Colonies on the eastern seaboard of North America who remained loyal to the British Empire during the American Revolution.
Short for United Empire Loyalist, such colonists who migrated to Canada.

d.x: The old dog loyally followed his master even if he didn't really want to go out.

d.d: The state of being loyal; fidelity.
Faithfulness or devotion to some person, cause or nation.
d.x: He showed loyalty to his local football club after successive relegations.
